title: Question-Based Learning Graph Update
description: Interactive visualization demonstrating how answering assessment questions updates a personal student learning graph with color-coded mastery states (unknown, mastered, ready-to-learn, learning-goal)
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Adaptive Assessment
Learning Graphs
Intelligent Tutoring Systems
Knowledge State Estimation
Personalized Learning
technicalRequirements: Modern web browser with JavaScript enabled
learningObjectives: Distinguish the four mastery states of a personal learning graph node: unknown (gray), mastered (green), ready-to-learn (orange), and learning goal (red)
Explain backward inference, in which mastering Two-Step Equations marks its prerequisites as mastered with certainty decaying 90% per level to 90%, 81%, and 73%
Explain forward propagation, in which a concept becomes ready-to-learn only once every one of its prerequisites has turned green
Predict how the colors of the 17 Algebra 1 nodes change after a correct or incorrect answer on a given concept, then verify by clicking that node
Evaluate why an adaptive assessment can skip questions on foundation concepts such as Number and Variable once a downstream concept is answered correctly
